Reproducing Johnson et al. (2019) from CRCNS data set fcx-3¶

Paper. Johnson EL, King-Stephens D, Weber PB, Laxer KD, Lin JJ, Knight RT (2019). Spectral imprints of working memory for everyday associations in the frontoparietal network. Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience 12, 65. doi:10.3389/fnsys.2018.00065. The claims file was written from the version of record (PMC6333050, open access); the paper has no supplement.

Data set. CRCNS fcx-3, doi:10.6080/K06971S9, read from the public bucket crcnsarchive under fcx-3/live/. CRCNS data sets are not versioned, so the version is recorded as unversioned (docs/archives.md). The paper cites no version; live/ is the only copy the bucket holds (there is no old/), with its files dated 2026-02-11 and the data description version 0.5 of 2019-01-04, the original version. The MD5 sums of the files read, from the data set's checksums.md5, are printed below, so that a later change is detectable.

What the data set holds. For each of the 7 subjects: the filtered continuous iEEG (data_primary.mat), channel names, electrode positions, the preprocessed epochs (data_derived.mat: pretrial, encoding and maintenance, and processing epochs of every channel kept, with a per-trial table of accuracy, condition, delay and RT) and a trial table with the epoch start samples. The docs list the analysed channels and give per-subject accuracy and RT. The paper's MATLAB scripts (analysis_scripts.zip) are deposited with the data and are read here for method details the paper leaves open (cited by file name).

Claims (claims/crcns-fcx-3/10.3389-fnsys.2018.00065.yaml), all tested:

Claim Tested on
table1-electrodes channel list of the docs and the derived epochs
trial-counts derived epochs and trial tables
fig1b-accuracy, fig1b-rt-identity-slower docs/summary_file.csv and trial tables
erp-no-condition-difference derived processing epochs
fig2-spatial-power, fig3-temporal-power, power-difficulty-subjects, power-low-frequencies derived processing epochs
fig4-maintenance-parietal-led, fig4a-delta-theta-shift, fig4c-alpha-beta-shift, directional-pairs derived maintenance and processing epochs
fig5a-delta-theta-epochs, fig5a-identity-direction, fig5a-spatiotemporal-bidirectional, fig5b-alpha-beta-no-sustained derived processing epochs

The data set's files are tar.gz archives (0.5 to 3.6 GB each), which cannot be read at random: each is streamed once, decompressed in memory, reduced to what the claims use, and released. The loading cell, which streams and analyses each subject in turn, takes nearly the whole run, 39 to 42 minutes of 40 to 43 in three runs.

CHAN = fcx3.channel_table()
SUMMARY = fcx3.summary_file()
META, RES = {}, {}
started = time.time()
for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS:
    t0 = time.time()
    chan = CHAN[CHAN.subject == sid].reset_index(drop=True)
    META[sid], RES[sid] = fcx3.load_subject(sid, chan)
    print(f"{sid}: streamed and analysed in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s", flush=True)
print(f"all subjects in {(time.time() - started) / 60:.1f} min")

The description says the derived structures have fsample: 1000; S7's say 512, as its sampling rate. The derived epochs carry every channel kept after preprocessing (29 to 155 per subject), of which the docs' channel list names 187 analysed channels in all (Table 1 gives 192; see table1-electrodes); only those are kept here. The continuous data (hdr nSamples) of the derived files have a different length from the deposited data_primary in S7 only. S3's elec_labels.mat is a MATLAB 5 file, the others MATLAB 7.3.

Task timing (Methods, Behavioral Task): pretrial 1 s, start screen 0.8 s, fixation 0.1 s, stimuli 2 x 0.2 s, delay 0.9 or 1.15 s, cue 0.8 s.

The description says the trial table lists each trial; in S6 and S7 it lists only the trials kept after artifact rejection (101 and 90 of 120, numbered up to 120), and in S1 to S5 all 120. The pretrial start (G) precedes the encoding start (H) by 1.9 s in every trial (1.87 to 1.92 s in S7, sampled at 512 Hz), the pretrial fixation and start screen and fixation of the Methods (1.0 + 0.8 + 0.1 s). The processing start (I) follows H by 1.4 s plus the delay, which fits an encoding epoch of 0.6 s (the description's "600 ms + jitter") and a 0.8-s cue.

print("Derived epochs located in the continuous data (step 1: search; step 2: every analysed channel at the found offset).")
rows = []
for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS:
    ck = META[sid]["clock"]
    ch = ck["channels"]
    num = ch.apply(lambda r: fcx3.split_label(r.channel)[1] - fcx3.split_label(r.reference)[1]
                   if fcx3.split_label(r.channel)[0] == fcx3.split_label(r.reference)[0] else None, axis=1)
    rows.append({"subject": sid, **{f"offset {k[5:]} (s)": round(v, 3) for k, v in ck["offsets_s"].items()},
                 "search r min": round(ck["search"].r.min(), 4),
                 "channels": len(ch), "r min": round(ch.r.min(), 4), "r median": round(ch.r.median(), 5),
                 "traces per channel": int(ch.n_traces.min()),
                 "reference = contact - k, k": dict(pd.Series(num).value_counts())})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

Each derived trace is the difference of the channel's contact and one other contact of the continuous data (correlation at least the minimum printed, over 8 random trials and all three epochs), so the derived channels are bipolar, labelled by one of their contacts. The reference is the contact numbered one above or below on strips and depth leads, and the next row of the grid on S3's 16 x 16 grid (16 below) and S6's 8 x 8 grid (8 below). The derived epochs start 1.4 s (pretrial), 1.5 s (encoding) and 1.8 s (processing) before the trial table's columns, in every subject, so their time axes are: pretrial, 0 at G + 0.1 s; encoding, 0 at H; processing, 0 at I - 0.3 s. The deposited scripts' windows are therefore the paper's: baseline [0.65, 0.85] s of the pretrial epoch is G + 0.75 to G + 0.95 s, 250 to 50 ms before the start screen; maintenance [0.6, 1.5] s of the encoding epoch is 0.9 s from H + 0.6 s; processing [0.3, 1.2] s is the 0.9 s from I. This shows that the derived data, the continuous data and the trial table share one clock. Whether the table's columns mark the screen events is checked next.

print("Timing contrast between 900-ms and 1150-ms delay trials (70-150 Hz amplitude; see fcx3.jitter_check).")
print("If the columns mark the events, the best shift is near 0 in every window; a shift beyond the shuffled maximum, with r")
print("above the shuffled maximum, means the events lie at different times relative to the column in the two groups.")
rows = []
for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS:
    for k, v in META[sid]["jitter"].items():
        rows.append({"subject": sid, "epoch": k, "window (s)": fcx3.JITTER_WINDOWS[k], "shift 1150 vs 900 (s)": round(v["lag_s"], 3),
                     "r": round(v["r"], 2), "shuffled max |shift|": round(v["shuffled_abs_lag_max_s"], 3),
                     "shuffled max r": round(v["shuffled_r_max"], 2)})
jit = pd.DataFrame(rows)
jit["clear"] = (jit["r"] > jit["shuffled max r"]) & (jit["shift 1150 vs 900 (s)"].abs() > jit["shuffled max |shift|"])
print(jit.to_string(index=False))

# cue-locked 70-150 Hz amplitude (mean over channels and trials) per delay group, the traces behind the timing contrast above
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(fcx3.SUBJECTS), 3, figsize=(13, 2.0 * len(fcx3.SUBJECTS)), sharex="col")
for i, sid in enumerate(fcx3.SUBJECTS):
    for j, key in enumerate(fcx3.JITTER_WINDOWS):
        v = META[sid]["jitter"][key]
        ax = axes[i, j]
        ax.plot(v["time"], v["trace_900"], color="tab:blue", lw=1, label="900-ms delay")
        ax.plot(v["time"], v["trace_1150"], color="tab:orange", lw=1, label="1150-ms delay")
        for x in {"data_pre": (), "data_encmain": (), "data_proc": (-0.5, 0.3)}[key]:
            ax.axvline(x, color="0.5", lw=0.6, ls=":")
        ax.axvspan(*fcx3.JITTER_WINDOWS[key], color="0.92", zorder=0)
        if key == "data_proc":
            ax.axvspan(*fcx3.PROC_WIN, color="tab:green", alpha=0.08, zorder=0)
        ax.set_title(f"{sid} {key}", fontsize=8)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
axes[0, 0].legend(fontsize=7)
for ax in axes[-1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("time in the derived epoch (s)", fontsize=8)
fig.suptitle("70-150 Hz amplitude / its mean; grey: window of the contrast; dotted: test cue on and off (data_proc); green: processing window", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

The test is weak where the 70-150 Hz response is small; the column "clear" marks the windows where the shift found exceeds every shuffled one and the alignment is better than every shuffled one. In the traces, S4's response to the stimuli and to the test cue comes about 0.25 s later in the 1150-ms trials, relative to the columns, in the encoding and processing epochs. The shifts of S2 and S3 in the processing epoch (table) are small by eye, and in the other subjects the 70-150 Hz response is small. If the processing columns of 1150-ms trials lie about 0.25 s before the events, the processing window of those trials would hold the end of the cue. The ERP and power tests and the task-induced PSI are therefore also run on the trials with a 900-ms delay only (configuration methods_900, and interval processing_900 for PSI), whose windows are not in question. With about half the trials these tests have less power, so power is also run on a random draw of trials of both delays with as many trials per condition (methods_half), which separates the loss of trials from the timing.

The 'distance' reading places each bipolar channel at the midpoint of its two contacts, taking contact n as the n-th electrode of the grid named by the label's prefix in the subject's _MNI_grid.csv (S3's RH1 to RH256 are its 256-contact grid HD_Grid); the files do not say how contacts are numbered on a grid, so this placement is an assumption, and with the stated 10-mm spacings 1.5 x spacing takes in diagonal neighbours on a grid.

The deposited scripts settle some details and not others, as printed above. They hold no cluster test (no FieldTrip statistics call, no neighbour definition, no cluster alpha), so the neighbour rule and the alpha per tail are open in the paper and in the code alike; every reading is run. power_compute.m and psi_compute.m compute the time-frequency windows over the whole derived epoch (cfg.toi from its first to its last sample) and cut the processing window afterwards, so their long windows take in data around the segment, while the Methods describe the 900-ms segments "zero-padded to 7,500 ms". Where the Methods and the code differ, the Methods come first: the zero-padded segment is the main reading here, and the code's whole-epoch windows are a variant. erp_compute.m low-passes the whole epoch and subtracts the baseline mean over trials, one value per channel, which cannot change a t-test. psianalysis.m z-scores the mean of per-trial PSI against a null built from the trial-mean spectrum, a different statistic, and omits the conjugate of the cross-spectrum; the PSI null used here follows the Methods' wording instead ("shuffled the frequencies in one signal and re-computed PSI"), and the code's null is shown as a variant.

table1-electrodes¶

The analysed data comprise 192 bipolar virtual electrodes in seven subjects, 4 to 54 (mean 19) in PFC and 2 to 16 (mean 8) in parietal cortex per subject, as listed per subject in Table 1, forming 1129 same-hemisphere PFC-parietal pairs.

Counted from docs/summary_channel_analysis.csv (every listed channel is in the derived epochs, or loading would have failed), with Table 1 typed from the paper for the comparison.

Result: partially reproduced. The data set's channel list holds 187 analysed channels, not 192: S4 has 5 right parietal channels where Table 1 gives 10; every other subject's counts and hemispheres equal Table 1. PFC counts per subject are 4 to 54 (mean 19.00) and parietal 2 to 16 (mean 7.71), both within tolerance. The list gives 1135 same-hemisphere pairs, 6 more than the paper's 1129 (+0.5%); with Table 1's 10 parietal channels in S4 it would give 1165. The totals differ by no more than 10% (channels -2.6%), the criterion's partial match.

trial-counts¶

After artifact rejection subjects kept on average 96 correct trials, 32 +- 3 (26 to 35) identity, 33 +- 4 (27 to 39) spatial and 31 +- 6 (20 to 39) temporal, and had 17 +- 8 (4 to 25) incorrect trials per subject.

Correct trials kept are those of the derived epochs with accuracy 1 (trialinfo column 2, the selection of the deposited scripts). The incorrect count is read (a) of all 120 trials, from the per-subject accuracy of docs/summary_file.csv (over all 120 trials, by the data description; 40 trials per condition, Methods), and (b) of the trials kept.

In S1 to S5 every correct trial of the 120 was kept.

fig1b-accuracy¶

All subjects were proficient at the task (accuracy 0.63 to 0.98, chance 0.5), and accuracy did not differ between conditions.

Accuracy per subject and condition is in docs/summary_file.csv, over all 120 trials (data description), which is reading (a) of B1's "all trials" question; the trial tables of S6 and S7 list only kept trials, so single-trial accuracy over all 120 is rebuilt as counts out of 40 per condition (Methods: "120 trials divided evenly"). The logit mixed model (condition fixed, subject random intercept) is fitted by maximum likelihood with Gauss-Hermite quadrature (fcx3.logit_mixed; the paper names the model, not the software), with condition as one numeric term (the single degree of freedom of the paper's F(1,19) for RT) and, as a variant, as two dummy terms. Reading (b) of B1 (accuracy over kept trials) is shown as a variant.

In [12]:

lo, hi = 0.63, 0.98

Result: reproduced. Under reading (b), per subject and condition, accuracy runs from 0.625 to 0.975, the paper's 0.63 to 0.98; under reading (a), per subject, it runs from 0.758 to 0.950, and the lowest value is outside 0.63 +- 0.063. The logit mixed model on all 120 trials finds no effect of condition (likelihood ratio p = 0.283 with condition as one term, p = 0.160 as two terms; kept trials p = 0.276), so the absence holds by the criterion (p > 0.05). The paper reports p > 0.50; the p obtained here is lower than that.

fig1b-rt-identity-slower¶

Response times differed by condition, being longer on identity than on spatial and temporal trials, with no difference between spatial and temporal trials.

Reading (a) of B1: one mean correct-trial RT per subject and condition (docs/summary_file.csv, "calculated on all correct trials"), a linear mixed model with condition as one numeric term and a subject random intercept (REML, statsmodels), F = t^2 on the residual degrees of freedom (21 - 2 = 19; pairs 14 - 2 = 12), as fitlme reports. Reading (b): single correct trials; only the kept trials are in the trial tables (all correct trials in S1 to S5), so (b) is on those. Cohen's d is given as the mean paired difference over its SD across subjects, one common definition (the paper does not say which it used; d is reported, not judged).

import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

rt = SUMMARY.melt(id_vars="subject", value_vars=["rt_identity", "rt_spatial", "rt_temporal"], var_name="cond", value_name="rt")
rt["c"] = rt.cond.map({"rt_identity": 1, "rt_spatial": 2, "rt_temporal": 3})
print(SUMMARY[["subject", "rt_identity", "rt_spatial", "rt_temporal"]].round(0).to_string(index=False))


def lme_f(df, y, groups):
    r = smf.mixedlm(f"{y} ~ c", df, groups=df[groups]).fit(reml=True)
    t = r.tvalues["c"]
    return r.params["c"], t ** 2, stats.f.sf(t ** 2, 1, len(df) - 2), len(df) - 2


def report(df, y, groups, label):
    out = {}
    b, F, p, dfr = lme_f(df, y, groups)
    out["all"] = (b, F, p)
    print(f"{label} omnibus: slope {b:.1f} ms per condition step, F(1,{dfr}) = {F:.2f}, p = {p:.4f}")
    for a, bb, name in [(1, 2, "identity vs spatial"), (1, 3, "identity vs temporal"), (2, 3, "spatial vs temporal")]:
        sub = df[df.c.isin([a, bb])].copy()
        b2, F2, p2, dfr2 = lme_f(sub, y, groups)
        out[name] = (b2, F2, p2)
        print(f"   {name}: difference {b2 * (bb - a):.1f} ms ({'first longer' if b2 < 0 else 'second longer'}), F(1,{dfr2}) = {F2:.2f}, p = {p2:.4f}")
    return out


rt_a = report(rt, "rt", "subject", "(a) subject-condition means")
w = SUMMARY.set_index("subject")
for a, b in [("rt_identity", "rt_spatial"), ("rt_identity", "rt_temporal"), ("rt_spatial", "rt_temporal")]:
    d = w[a] - w[b]
    print(f"   d ({a[3:]} - {b[3:]}): {d.mean() / d.std(ddof=1):.2f}; identity longer in {int((d > 0).sum())}/7 subjects")
tr = kept[kept.correct == 1].rename(columns={"condition": "c"})
rt_b = report(tr, "rt", "subject", "(b) single kept correct trials")

Result: reproduced. On subject-condition means (reading (a)), condition affects RT (F(1,19) = 6.04, p = 0.024), identity RT is longer than spatial (by 513 ms, F(1,12) = 11.81, p = 0.005) and temporal (by 392 ms, F(1,12) = 9.39, p = 0.010), and spatial and temporal do not differ (p = 0.254). Identity RT is the longest in all 7 subjects. The F values are below the paper's bounds (F > 6.50, > 13.78, > 10.95), and the d values (1.30, 1.16, by the definition used here) below its 2.14 and 1.91. Single kept trials (reading (b)) give the same pattern (p = 0.018, 0.037, 0.004 and 0.844).

erp-no-condition-difference¶

ERPs over the processing interval did not differ between identity and spatial or temporal trials in any subject.

Main reading, per the claim's criterion and the Methods (Event-Related Potentials, paragraph 1): the 200-ms pretrial baseline and 900-ms processing segments are cut, each zero padded to 7.5 s and low-passed at 30 Hz (FIR), and the baseline is the pretrial temporal mean averaged over trials, as erp_compute.m computes it (one value per channel, which cannot change a t-test). Variants: each trial corrected on its own pretrial mean (the Methods' "post-cue processing - pretrial mean" allows it); the Results' "1-30 Hz bandpass" in place of the low-pass; the whole derived epoch filtered before the windows are cut (erp_compute.m); the main reading on the 900-ms-delay trials only (Data check). Each is tested per subject by the cluster test of S2 over channels and time, identity against spatial and against temporal, 1000 shuffles. Readings of the neighbours: adjacent, distance, none; readings of the threshold: a cluster's p below 0.05 per tail (the Methods' "fewer than 5% of randomizations yielded a larger effect", and FieldTrip's behaviour when cfg.alpha = 0.05 and the tails are not corrected), or below 0.025. The deposited scripts hold no cluster test, so neither is settled by the code. The smallest cluster p per subject and contrast is printed for each. With 1000 shuffles a cluster p near 0.04 has a Monte Carlo standard error of about 0.006.

Result: not reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under the main reading with neighbours adjacent by contact number and clusters judged at 0.05 per tail, S2 has a significant cluster for identity against temporal (p = 0.041); no other subject-contrast is below 0.05, and 2 of 14 have p <= 0.10 (the paper reports all p > 0.10). The outcome depends on the readings: at 0.025 per tail the adjacent reading finds no significant cluster (reproduced), while the distance reading (S5, p = 0.014) and the reading without spatial clustering (S2, p = 0.024) find one at either threshold. Among the variants, the 1-30 Hz band-pass gives no cluster below 0.05 with adjacent neighbours (smallest p 0.085); the per-trial baseline gives one (S5 identity against spatial, p = 0.030); filtering the whole epoch gives S2 p = 0.031; the 900-ms-delay trials alone give one (S5 identity against temporal, p = 0.023). Under the adopted reading the deciding p (0.041) is close to 0.05, so a different Monte Carlo draw could move it to either side; the distance reading's p = 0.014 is not close to the threshold.

fig2-spatial-power and fig3-temporal-power¶

In the identity against spatial contrast of processing-interval power, 5 of 7 subjects showed spatial > identity effects (54 +- 22% of electrodes per subject) and 2 of 7 showed identity > spatial effects (36 +- 12%).

In the identity against temporal contrast of processing-interval power, 4 of 7 subjects showed temporal > identity effects (68 +- 30% of electrodes per subject) and 2 of 7 showed identity > temporal effects (37 +- 10%).

Power with 3-cycle Hanning windows, 2 to 40 Hz, 10-ms steps over the 900-ms processing segment. Main reading: the segment alone, embedded in zeros, every window computed (Methods, Spectral Decomposition, "Data segments were zero-padded to 7,500 ms"; S1 reading (a)). Variant: the windows computed on the whole derived epoch and the processing window cut afterwards, as power_compute.m does (its lines are printed in the Data check), so that windows longer than the segment (below about 3.3 Hz) take in the cue and the response period. A further variant uses the main reading on the 900-ms-delay trials only. Power is z-scored on the bootstrapped pretrial baseline of all correct trials (zbaseline.m; r = all correct trials, settling S1's open r), which cannot change the t-tests. The cluster test of S2 over channel, frequency and time, 1000 shuffles. An electrode shows an effect of a sign when any of its points lies in a significant cluster of that sign (S2 reading (a)); reading (b) assigns an electrode in both to the sign with the larger summed t. Every combination of spectra, neighbour reading, threshold and assignment is shown, and the per-subject percentages under each reading.

In [15]:
def power_effects(contrast, nb, alpha=0.05, assign="a", config="methods"):
    out = []
    for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS:
        cl = RES[sid]["power"][config][contrast]["clusters"][nb]
        n = len(RES[sid]["labels"])
        ident, other = np.zeros(n, bool), np.zeros(n, bool)
        ts_i, ts_o = np.zeros(n), np.zeros(n)
        for c in cl["pos"]:  # positive t: identity > other
            if c["p"] < alpha:
                ident |= c["elec_mask"]
                ts_i += c["tsum_by_elec"]
        for c in cl["neg"]:
            if c["p"] < alpha:
                other |= c["elec_mask"]
                ts_o += -c["tsum_by_elec"]
        if assign == "b":
            both = ident & other
            ident = ident & ~(both & (ts_o >= ts_i))
            other = other & ~(both & (ts_i > ts_o))
        out.append({"subject": sid, "n": n, "other>identity": int(other.sum()), "identity>other": int(ident.sum()),
                    "p other>identity": cl["neg_minp"], "p identity>other": cl["pos_minp"]})
    return pd.DataFrame(out)


POWER_LABEL = {"methods": "segment zero-padded (main)", "code": "whole-epoch windows (power_compute.m)",
               "methods_900": "segment zero-padded, 900-ms-delay trials only",
               "methods_half": "segment zero-padded, random trials of both delays, as many per condition as methods_900 (control)"}
EXPECTED = {"spatial": (5, 2, 54, 36), "temporal": (4, 2, 68, 37)}
POWER_SUMMARY = []
PER_SUBJECT = {}
for config in fcx3.POWER_CONFIGS:
    for contrast in ["spatial", "temporal"]:
        for nb in fcx3.NB_READINGS:
            for alpha in (0.05, 0.025):
                for assign in ("a", "b"):
                    e = power_effects(contrast, nb, alpha, assign, config)
                    po = 100 * e["other>identity"] / e.n
                    pi = 100 * e["identity>other"] / e.n
                    PER_SUBJECT[(config, contrast, nb, alpha, assign)] = [f"{a:.0f}/{b:.0f}" for a, b in zip(po, pi)]
                    so, si = po[po > 0], pi[pi > 0]
                    ex = EXPECTED[contrast]
                    row = {"config": config, "contrast": contrast, "neighbours": nb, "alpha per tail": alpha, "assign": assign,
                           "subjects other>id": len(so), "subjects id>other": len(si),
                           "% other>id": f"{so.mean():.1f} +- {so.std(ddof=1):.1f}" if len(so) > 1 else (f"{so.mean():.1f}" if len(so) else "-"),
                           "% id>other": f"{si.mean():.1f} +- {si.std(ddof=1):.1f}" if len(si) > 1 else (f"{si.mean():.1f}" if len(si) else "-"),
                           "subjects other>id (list)": list(e.subject[po > 0]), "subjects id>other (list)": list(e.subject[pi > 0])}
                    row["counts match"] = len(so) == ex[0] and len(si) == ex[1]
                    row["% match"] = (len(so) > 0 and len(si) > 0 and abs(so.mean() - ex[2]) <= 0.1 * ex[2]
                                      and abs(si.mean() - ex[3]) <= 0.1 * ex[3])
                    row["counts within 1"] = abs(len(so) - ex[0]) <= 1 and abs(len(si) - ex[1]) <= 1
                    POWER_SUMMARY.append(row)
POWER_SUMMARY = pd.DataFrame(POWER_SUMMARY)
for config in fcx3.POWER_CONFIGS:
    print(f"==== {config}: {POWER_LABEL[config]}")
    print(POWER_SUMMARY[POWER_SUMMARY.config == config].drop(columns=["config", "subjects other>id (list)", "subjects id>other (list)"]).to_string(index=False))
print("\nSubjects per effect, main spectra, 0.05 per tail, assignment (a):")
print(POWER_SUMMARY[(POWER_SUMMARY.config == "methods") & (POWER_SUMMARY["alpha per tail"] == 0.05) & (POWER_SUMMARY["assign"] == "a")][
    ["contrast", "neighbours", "subjects other>id (list)", "subjects id>other (list)"]].to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. Under the main spectra, 5 subjects show spatial > identity effects (S2 to S6) under every neighbour reading and threshold, and 1 shows identity > spatial effects (S4; paper 2) under every reading but adjacent neighbours at 0.025 per tail, which finds none. With adjacent neighbours at 0.05 per tail the percentages are 37.7 +- 21.1% and 11.8% (S4 alone), below the paper's 54 +- 22% and 36 +- 12%. The counts match within one subject and 5 of 7 subjects have a significant cluster, the criterion's partial match. The paper's counts (5 and 2) appear only with the whole-epoch windows of power_compute.m, where S7 adds an identity > spatial effect; there the distance reading gives 52.0% (within tolerance of 54) and 28.4% (outside tolerance of 36), so no reading matches both percentages. The significant clusters of the main spectra have p <= 0.028. On the 900-ms-delay trials alone 2 or 3 subjects show spatial > identity effects and none identity > spatial. A random draw of as many trials from both delays loses about as much (1 to 3 subjects spatial > identity, 0 or 1 identity > spatial), so the loss on the 900-ms trials comes from having fewer trials and does not show that the effects depend on the 1150-ms trials' timing; with half the trials these tests cannot settle it either way, here or for power-difficulty-subjects, which rests on the same effects.

Result: partially reproduced. Under the main spectra, adjacent neighbours, 0.05 per tail and assignment (a), 5 subjects show temporal > identity effects (paper 4) and 2 identity > temporal effects (S1, S7; paper 2), with 37.4 +- 20.5% and 21.0 +- 17.4% of electrodes (paper 68 +- 30% and 37 +- 10%). Assignment (b) gives the paper's counts, 4 and 2, with 41.2% and 21.0%. No reading of spectra, neighbours, threshold or assignment brings both percentages within tolerance; the distance reading gives 47.8 to 55.2% for temporal > identity. The significant clusters of the reported effects have p <= 0.014 with adjacent neighbours, except S2, whose temporal > identity cluster is significant only under the distance reading (p = 0.020) and without spatial clustering (p = 0.044). On the 900-ms-delay trials alone 1 to 3 subjects show temporal > identity effects and 1 (S1) identity > temporal; the random draw of as many trials from both delays gives 2 or 3 and 0 or 1, as for fig2-spatial-power.

power-difficulty-subjects¶

The subjects with identity > spatial or temporal power effects were the same subjects who had both longer RTs and lower accuracy on identity trials.

Subjects with an identity > spatial or identity > temporal effect are taken from the power claims (every spectra, neighbour and threshold reading, assignment (a)); accuracy (all 120 trials) and mean correct RT per condition from docs/summary_file.csv.

w = SUMMARY.copy()
w["subject"] = w.subject.str.lower()
w = w.set_index("subject")
beh = pd.DataFrame({
    "RT id > sp": w.rt_identity > w.rt_spatial, "acc id < sp": w.acc_identity < w.acc_spatial,
    "RT id > tp": w.rt_identity > w.rt_temporal, "acc id < tp": w.acc_identity < w.acc_temporal,
    "RT id > mean(sp,tp)": w.rt_identity > (w.rt_spatial + w.rt_temporal) / 2,
    "acc id < mean(sp,tp)": w.acc_identity < (w.acc_spatial + w.acc_temporal) / 2})
beh["both (a) spatial"] = beh["RT id > sp"] & beh["acc id < sp"]
beh["both (a) temporal"] = beh["RT id > tp"] & beh["acc id < tp"]
beh["both (b)"] = beh["RT id > mean(sp,tp)"] & beh["acc id < mean(sp,tp)"]
print(beh.to_string())
for config in fcx3.POWER_CONFIGS:
    for nb in fcx3.NB_READINGS:
        for alpha in (0.05, 0.025):
            sel = POWER_SUMMARY[(POWER_SUMMARY.config == config) & (POWER_SUMMARY.neighbours == nb) & (POWER_SUMMARY["alpha per tail"] == alpha)
                                & (POWER_SUMMARY["assign"] == "a")].set_index("contrast")
            sp_ = set(sel.loc["spatial", "subjects id>other (list)"])
            tp_ = set(sel.loc["temporal", "subjects id>other (list)"])
            effect = sorted(sp_ | tp_)
            ok_a = all((s not in sp_ or beh.loc[s, "both (a) spatial"]) and (s not in tp_ or beh.loc[s, "both (a) temporal"]) for s in effect)
            ok_b = all(beh.loc[s, "both (b)"] for s in effect)
            others_a = [s for s in beh.index if s not in effect and (beh.loc[s, "both (a) spatial"] or beh.loc[s, "both (a) temporal"])]
            others_b = [s for s in beh.index if s not in effect and beh.loc[s, "both (b)"]]
            print(f"{config}, {nb}, {alpha}: identity>spatial {sorted(sp_)}, identity>temporal {sorted(tp_)}; every one has both under (a): {ok_a},"
                  f" under (b): {ok_b}; other subjects with both, (a): {others_a}, (b): {others_b}")

Result: reproduced. Under the main spectra the subjects with identity > spatial or temporal effects are S1, S4 and S7 under every neighbour reading at 0.05 per tail (S4 for spatial, S1 and S7 for temporal, and S4 also for temporal without spatial clustering). Under reading (b), identity against the mean of spatial and temporal, each has longer identity RT and lower identity accuracy; under reading (a) S1 fails for the temporal contrast, where its identity and temporal accuracy are equal (0.825). The same holds under every other configuration printed. S3 also has both without an identity > effect, so the converse ("the same subjects", reading (ii)) does not hold. Identity RT is the longest in all 7 subjects, so only accuracy separates subjects here.

power-low-frequencies¶

Significant processing-interval power effects were most prominent at low frequencies, in distinct delta-theta (2 to 7 Hz) and alpha-beta (9 to 24 Hz) ranges, whatever the contrast.

Per subject and effect, the t values inside significant clusters (0.05 per tail) are averaged over electrodes and time per frequency, (a) over the masked points only, (b) over all points with the unmasked as zero; then averaged, in absolute value, over the subjects with the effect. The rule (2-24 Hz larger than 25-40 Hz, local maxima in 2-7 and 9-24 Hz) is the claims file's. A point at either end of the 2-40 Hz range counts as a local maximum when it exceeds its one neighbour (the usual definition on a closed range); the result without counting the 2-Hz end is shown as well. Every neighbour reading is shown, for the main spectra and the whole-epoch variant.

In [18]:
def density(nb, effect, reading, alpha=0.05, config="methods"):
    out = {}
    for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS:
        R = RES[sid]
        dens = []
        for contrast in (["spatial"] if effect == "spatial>identity" else ["temporal"] if effect == "temporal>identity" else ["spatial", "temporal"]):
            cl = R["power"][config][contrast]["clusters"][nb]
            sign = "neg" if effect != "identity>other" else "pos"
            cs = [c for c in cl[sign] if c["p"] < alpha]
            if not cs:
                continue
            tm = sum(c["t_masked"].astype(float) for c in cs)  # ch x f x t
            if reading == "a":
                cnt = (tm != 0).sum(axis=(0, 2))
                dens.append(np.where(cnt > 0, tm.sum(axis=(0, 2)) / np.maximum(cnt, 1), 0))
            else:
                dens.append(tm.mean(axis=(0, 2)))
        if dens:
            out[sid] = np.abs(np.mean(dens, axis=0))
    return out


f = fcx3.FOI
LF = []
for config in ("methods", "code"):
    for nb in fcx3.NB_READINGS:
        for reading in ("a", "b"):
            for effect in ["spatial>identity", "temporal>identity", "identity>other"]:
                d = density(nb, effect, reading, config=config)
                if not d:
                    LF.append({"config": config, "neighbours": nb, "reading": reading, "effect": effect, "subjects": 0})
                    continue
                m = np.mean(list(d.values()), axis=0)
                low, high = m[(f >= 2) & (f <= 24)].mean(), m[(f >= 25) & (f <= 40)].mean()
                peaks = [int(f[i]) for i in range(len(f)) if (i == 0 or m[i] > m[i - 1]) and (i == len(f) - 1 or m[i] >= m[i + 1])]
                inner = [p for p in peaks if 2 < p < 40]
                LF.append({"config": config, "neighbours": nb, "reading": reading, "effect": effect, "subjects": len(d), "2-24 Hz": round(low, 3),
                           "25-40 Hz": round(high, 3), "low > high": low > high, "local maxima (Hz)": peaks,
                           "max in 2-7": any(2 <= p <= 7 for p in peaks), "max in 9-24": any(9 <= p <= 24 for p in peaks),
                           "max in 2-7, 2-Hz edge not counted": any(2 < p <= 7 for p in inner), "peak Hz": int(f[np.argmax(m)])})
LF = pd.DataFrame(LF)
print(LF.to_string(index=False))
ok = LF[LF.subjects > 0].groupby(["config", "neighbours", "reading"]).apply(
    lambda g: pd.Series({"all three meet the rule": bool((g["low > high"] & g["max in 2-7"] & g["max in 9-24"]).all() and len(g) == 3),
                         "same, 2-Hz edge not counted": bool((g["low > high"] & g["max in 2-7, 2-Hz edge not counted"] & g["max in 9-24"]).all() and len(g) == 3)}))

Result: reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under the main spectra with the density over all points (reading (b)), every neighbour reading meets the rule. With adjacent neighbours, each effect is larger over 2 to 24 Hz than over 25 to 40 Hz (0.099 against 0.021 for spatial > identity, 0.097 against 0.032 for temporal > identity, 0.057 against 0.018 for identity > other), with local maxima in 2 to 7 Hz (2, 3 and 2 Hz) and in 9 to 24 Hz. The match rests on counting the 2-Hz end of the range as a local maximum: without it, the identity > other density (maxima at 2 and 14 Hz) has no maximum in 2 to 7 Hz in any combination with reading (b), which would be the partial match. Over masked points only (reading (a)) the identity > other density is larger above 24 Hz under every combination. With the whole-epoch windows only the distance reading meets the rule.

Task-induced PSI: fig4-maintenance-parietal-led, fig4a-delta-theta-shift, fig4c-alpha-beta-shift, directional-pairs¶

During maintenance, PFC-parietal connectivity was unidirectional, parietal to PFC, in both the delta-theta (z < -40.03 +- 8.73) and alpha-beta (z < -30.37 +- 2.60) ranges.

After the test cue, delta-theta directionality shifted from a unidirectional parietal-led network to a bidirectional frontoparietal one, with net PFC-led connectivity above zero in 6 of 7 subjects during processing (z > 6.01 +- 6.42).

Alpha-beta directionality also shifted with the test cue, but all subjects remained net parietal-led during processing (z < -12.60 +- 7.51).

During processing, 1008 pairs were significantly directional in the delta-theta range and 984 in the alpha-beta range.

PSI per P1, with the details psi_compute.m and psianalysis.m settle: the ERP subtracted is the mean over all correct trials (P1 "raw trial-wise mean", reading (a); subtracterp.m with one condition); spectra are one Hanning-tapered FFT of each 900-ms segment padded to 7.5 s ('mtmfft', P1 spectra reading (a)); PSI is one value per band summed over adjacent 1-Hz bins (band reading (a)). PSI is computed (a) from the trial-averaged coherency (Nolte et al. 2008) or (b) per trial from the per-trial normalised cross-spectrum, averaged over trials (the structure of psianalysis.m), with the conjugate the Methods' cross-spectral density implies.

The null follows the Methods: "we randomly shuffled the frequencies in one signal and re-computed PSI 1,000 times". Each shuffle permutes the frequency bins of the parietal spectrum (the same permutation for every trial and pair, P1 null reading (a)) and recomputes the same statistic, so that the null and the observed value measure the same thing (fcx3.psi_z). psianalysis.m builds its null differently, from the slope of the trial-mean spectrum with both factors shuffled, which is not the statistic it z-scores; reading (b) against that null is shown as a variant (b_code). The deposited code without the conjugate, whose measure equals plus or minus exp(2i x the second channel's phase) and so depends on one channel only, is shown with either channel first for the record of that code mismatch; it is not a reading of the paper and decides no outcome. As a check of calibration on these data, each subject's processing PSI is also computed with the parietal trials paired with other trials' PFC data, which removes any trial-locked coupling; a calibrated z then exceeds 1.96 in about 5% of pairs. Positive z: PFC leads.

P1 also leaves open whether each shuffle permutes the bins in the same way for all trials (null reading (a), used above) or with its own permutation per trial (null reading (b)); both are run for readings (a) and (b) (a_trial, b_trial).

Which reading is adopted. Where the readings give different outcomes, reading (a) with null reading (a) is adopted: it is the first P1 lists, the measure of Nolte et al. (2008), and the one whose z is calibrated. On the trial-shuffled data below, its z has mean -0.05 (delta-theta) and 0.02 (alpha-beta), SD 1.01 and 1.04, and passes |z| > 1.96 in 6.0% and 6.9% of pairs. Reading (b) has mean -0.29 and SD 0.60 in delta-theta (0.1% of pairs pass), and its subject means on the trial-shuffled data run from -1.25 to 0.52 in alpha-beta, where the true value is 0. On independent synthetic signals (the cell after the calibration) its mean z is -0.21 to -0.37, where reading (a) gives -0.07 to -0.15 with SD near 1. Moving the FFT's time origin to the centre of the segment brings reading (b)'s mean to -0.06 to 0.12, which is consistent with the offset coming from the phase slope that each trial's spectrum carries from the segment's position in the padded window: the per-trial phasors of reading (b) keep it, the frequency shuffle breaks it, and the trial-averaged cross-spectrum of reading (a) cancels it. One permutation per trial does not help reading (b) (mean -0.51 in delta-theta, 17% of alpha-beta pairs past 1.96). The first revision adopted reading (b), for the structure of psianalysis.m; the second verification round found it uncalibrated. Three outcomes rested on it (fig4c-alpha-beta-shift, fig5a-spatiotemporal-bidirectional, fig5b-alpha-beta-no-sustained); the change that reading (a) gives was proposed for a third round, whose verifier agreed with all three, and they now rest on reading (a).

READ = {"a": "(a) trial-averaged coherency", "b": "(b) per-trial PSI averaged",
        "a_trial": "(a), one permutation per trial (P1 null (b))", "b_trial": "(b), one permutation per trial (P1 null (b))",
        "b_code": "(b) against psianalysis.m's null (variant)",
        "code": "deposited code, PFC first (not a reading)", "code_rev": "deposited code, parietal first, sign reversed (not a reading)"}
psi_rows = []
for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS:
    for band in fcx3.BANDS:
        for iv in ("maintenance", "processing", "processing_900"):
            zs = {**RES[sid]["psi"][band][iv], **RES[sid]["psi_deposited"][band].get(iv, {})}
            for k, z in zs.items():
                for (pfc, par, hemi), v in zip(RES[sid]["pairs"], z):
                    psi_rows.append({"subject": sid, "band": band, "interval": iv, "reading": k, "pair": f"{sid}:{pfc}-{par}", "z": v})
PSI = pd.DataFrame(psi_rows)
print("Pairs per subject:", PSI[(PSI.band == "delta-theta") & (PSI.interval == "maintenance") & (PSI.reading == "a")].groupby("subject").size().to_dict())
print("Frequencies read (Hz):", {b: np.round(RES[fcx3.SUBJECTS[0]]['psi'][b]['freqs'], 3).tolist() for b in fcx3.BANDS})
persub = PSI.groupby(["band", "interval", "reading", "subject"]).z.mean().unstack("subject")
print("\nPer-subject mean PSI z over pairs:")
print(persub.round(2).to_string())
grp = PSI.groupby(["band", "interval", "reading", "subject"]).z.mean().groupby(["band", "interval", "reading"]).agg(["mean", "std", "min", "max"])
grp.columns = ["mean over subjects", "SD over subjects", "min subject", "max subject"]
pairs_ = PSI.groupby(["band", "interval", "reading"]).z.agg(["mean", "std", "min", "max", lambda z: np.mean(np.abs(z) > 1.96)])
pairs_.columns = ["mean over pairs", "SD over pairs", "min pair", "max pair", "fraction |z| > 1.96"]
print("\n", pd.concat([grp, pairs_], axis=1).round(2).to_string())

print("Calibration on the data: processing PSI with each PFC trial paired with another trial's parietal data")
print("(trial order shuffled within subject, so no trial-locked coupling; a calibrated z has mean near 0, SD near 1, and |z| > 1.96 in about 5% of pairs)")
rows = []
SURMEAN = {}
for band in fcx3.BANDS:
    for k in ("a", "b", "a_trial", "b_trial", "b_code"):
        z = np.concatenate([RES[sid]["psi_surrogate"][band][k] for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS])
        by = {sid: round(float(np.mean(np.abs(RES[sid]["psi_surrogate"][band][k]) > 1.96)), 2) for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS}
        SURMEAN[(band, k)] = pd.Series({sid: float(np.mean(RES[sid]["psi_surrogate"][band][k])) for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS})
        rows.append({"band": band, "reading": READ[k], "pairs": len(z), "fraction |z| > 1.96": round(float(np.mean(np.abs(z) > 1.96)), 3),
                     "mean of z": round(float(z.mean()), 2), "SD of z": round(float(z.std()), 2), "|z| > 1.96 by subject": by})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))
print("\nSurrogate mean z per subject (over the subject's pairs):")
print(pd.DataFrame({f"{b} {k}": v for (b, k), v in SURMEAN.items() if k != "b_code"}).round(2).T.to_string())
print("Trials left in place by the shuffle:", {sid: RES[sid]["psi_surrogate"]["delta-theta"]["same_trial_fraction"] for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS})

# Calibration on synthetic data (no data set files): independent PFC and parietal signals, so the true PSI is 0.
# 33 trials of 1/f or 1/f^2 noise, 900-ms segments, the same FFT, ERP removal and null as above (300 shuffles here).
# 'b, segment centred' moves the FFT's time origin to the centre of the segment (a diagnostic, not a reading).
rng_s = np.random.default_rng(fcx3.seed("synthetic"))
fs_s, n_s = 1000, 1300
t_s = np.arange(n_s) / fs_s - 0.2


def noise(kind, n_tr, n_ch):
    w = rng_s.standard_normal((n_tr, n_ch, n_s))
    if kind == "1/f^2":
        return np.cumsum(w, -1)
    f = np.fft.rfftfreq(n_s, 1 / fs_s)
    f[0] = 1
    return np.fft.irfft(np.fft.rfft(w, axis=-1) / np.sqrt(f), n=n_s, axis=-1)


rows = []
for kind in ("1/f", "1/f^2"):
    for band, (lo, hi) in fcx3.BANDS.items():
        zs = {}
        for rep in range(40):
            x = np.concatenate([noise(kind, 33, 4), noise(kind, 33, 4)], 1)
            F, fr = fcx3.fft_segment(x, t_s, fs_s, (0.0, 0.9), np.arange(lo, hi + 1))
            F = F - F.mean(0, keepdims=True)
            ia_s, ib_s = np.repeat(np.arange(4), 4), np.tile(np.arange(4), 4)
            out = fcx3.psi_z(F[:, :4, :, None], F[:, 4:, :, None], ia_s, ib_s, rng_s, n_perm=300, trial_null=True)
            Fc = F * np.exp(2j * np.pi * fr * 0.45)  # origin at the segment's centre (0.45 s)
            out["b, segment centred"] = fcx3.psi_z(Fc[:, :4, :, None], Fc[:, 4:, :, None], ia_s, ib_s, rng_s, n_perm=300)["b"]
            for k, v in out.items():
                zs.setdefault(k, []).append(v[:, 0])
        for k, v in zs.items():
            v = np.concatenate(v)
            rows.append({"noise": kind, "band": band, "reading": READ.get(k, k), "mean of z": round(float(v.mean()), 2),
                         "SE of mean (by run)": round(float(np.std([np.mean(u) for u in zs[k]], ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(zs[k]))), 2),
                         "SD of z": round(float(v.std()), 2), "fraction |z| > 1.96": round(float(np.mean(np.abs(v) > 1.96)), 3)})
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

Result: not reproduced. Under no PSI reading is maintenance parietal-led in any subject. Under reading (a), adopted, subject means are -0.39 to 0.15 (delta-theta, mean -0.08 +- 0.20) and -0.67 to 0.04 (alpha-beta, -0.24 +- 0.25); under reading (b) -0.67 to 0.05 and -0.48 to -0.05; with one permutation per trial the lowest subject mean is -1.27; none is below -1.96. The paper reports -40.03 +- 8.73 and -30.37 +- 2.60. Against psianalysis.m's null, reading (b) puts 4 of 7 subjects below -1.96 in delta-theta (mean -0.31 +- 10.68) and none in alpha-beta, but that null gives |z| > 1.96 in 90% and 92% of trial-shuffled pairs, so it does not measure direction. The deposited code without the conjugate gives every subject below -1.96 with the parietal channel first (means -55.47 and -69.83) and above +1.96 with the PFC channel first (+58.67 and +69.48); its sign follows the channel order.

LME = {}
for band in fcx3.BANDS:
    for k in ("a", "b", "a_trial", "b_trial", "b_code", "code", "code_rev"):
        d = PSI[(PSI.band == band) & (PSI.reading == k)].pivot_table(index=["subject", "pair"], columns="interval", values="z").reset_index()
        eff, F, p, n = fcx3.paired_lme(d.maintenance.values, d.processing.values, d.subject.values)
        LME[(band, k)] = (eff, F, p, n)
        line = f"{band}, {READ[k]}: processing - maintenance {eff:.2f}, F(1,{2 * n - 2}) = {F:.1f}, p = {p:.3g} (pairs {n})"
        if k in ("a", "b"):
            e2, F2, p2 = fcx3.mixedlm_check(d.maintenance.values, d.processing.values, d.subject.values, d.pair.values)
            line += f"; statsmodels MixedLM: {e2:.2f}, F {F2:.1f}, p {p2:.3g}"
            # pairs share electrodes; a subject-level test does not treat them as independent
            ps = d.groupby("subject")[["maintenance", "processing"]].mean()
            tt = stats.ttest_rel(ps.processing, ps.maintenance)
            line += f"; subject means, paired t(6) = {tt.statistic:.2f}, p {tt.pvalue:.3g}"
        print(line)
print("Paper: delta-theta F(1,2256) = 1936.10, p < 8e-306; alpha-beta F(1,2256) = 2302.30, p = 0 (processing > maintenance).")

Result: not reproduced. No subject has net delta-theta PSI z above 0 in processing under any reading (means -0.17 +- 0.16 under reading (a), adopted, and -0.43 +- 0.34 under (b); -0.21 and -0.76 with one permutation per trial; paper 6.01 +- 6.42 with 6 subjects above 0). Processing exceeds maintenance in the pair-level model under reading (b) (by 0.27, F(1,2268) = 114.2, p = 4.9e-26; paper F = 1936.10) but not under reading (a) (0.06, F = 2.2, p = 0.14), and on subject means the difference is absent under both (paired t(6) p = 0.43 and 0.95). The criterion's partial match needs at least 4 subjects above 0. Against psianalysis.m's null, reading (b) gives 4 subjects above 0 (mean of those 6.36) and F = 58.5, but that null is not calibrated (trial-shuffled pairs pass |z| > 1.96 in 90% of cases). On the 900-ms-delay trials alone 2 (a) or 1 (b) subjects are above 0 (means -0.14 and -0.30).

Result: not reproduced, resting on PSI reading (a). Under reading (a), whose z is calibrated and which is adopted, 5 of 7 subjects have processing alpha-beta PSI z below 0 (mean -0.14 +- 0.26), fewer than the 6 the partial match needs, and processing is higher than maintenance by 0.11 in the pair-level model (F = 6.7, p = 0.0097; paper F = 2302.30); one permutation per trial gives the same 5 of 7. Observed minus the trial-shuffled surrogate is -0.01 +- 0.23 (p = 0.93). Under reading (b), 6 of 7 subjects are below 0 (S3 is above, 0.46) and processing exceeds maintenance (by 0.43, F(1,2268) = 97.9, p = 1.2e-22), which would be the partial match by the letter, but the outputs above show that this comes from reading (b)'s null. On the trial-shuffled data, which have no trial-locked coupling, reading (b) gives subject means of -1.17, -0.40, 0.52, -0.55, -0.60, -1.25 and 0.03 (S1 to S7), close to the observed -1.07, -0.51, 0.46, -0.61, -0.72, -1.35 and -0.18 (observed minus surrogate -0.08 +- 0.09, paired t(6) p = 0.061), and on synthetic independent signals reading (b)'s mean z is -0.25 to -0.29 in alpha-beta. The second verification round reviewed partially reproduced under reading (b); the change was proposed and the third round agreed. Subject means are -0.49 to 0.19 under (a) and -1.35 to 0.46 under (b), against the paper's -12.60 +- 7.51; on subject means the interval difference is not significant under either reading (paired t(6) p = 0.48 and 0.27). On the 900-ms-delay trials alone 4 (a) or 6 (b) subjects are below 0.

Result: not reproduced. With the Methods' null, 78 (reading (a), adopted) or 1 (reading (b)) of 1135 pairs have processing |z| > 1.96 in delta-theta, and 104 or 74 in alpha-beta, against the paper's 1008 and 984. The trial-shuffled surrogate gives 68 and 78 under (a) and 1 and 71 under (b), and a null at 5% would give about 57, so the counts are near what signals without trial-locked coupling give. With one permutation per trial the counts are 98 and 93 (a) and 78 and 211 (b), against 75 and 71, and 76 and 194, on the surrogate. Against psianalysis.m's null, reading (b) gives 1014 and 1041, within tolerance, but the trial-shuffled surrogate gives 1022 and 1044 under the same null, so that count does not reflect directionality. The deposited code as written (no conjugate) marks 1129 to 1135 of the 1135 pairs on the real data.

Time-resolved PSI: fig5a-delta-theta-epochs, fig5a-identity-direction, fig5a-spatiotemporal-bidirectional, fig5b-alpha-beta-no-sustained¶

Time-resolved delta-theta PSI differed between conditions in sustained epochs at 0 to 120 ms and 470 to 610 ms (identity against spatial) and at 0 to 170 ms and 660 to 860 ms (identity against temporal) after the test cue, the spatial late epoch ending about 50 ms before the temporal one begins.

In identity trials the PFC led parietal sites early in processing (z > 2.62 and z > 2.35 in the two contrasts' early epochs) and the parietal cortex led later (z < -3.04 and z < -3.57).

Delta-theta PSI during the selection of spatial and of temporal information stayed bidirectional (net near zero) throughout the processing interval.

Time-resolved alpha-beta PSI showed significant condition differences at some time points but no sustained effect for either condition in either contrast.

Per P2 and psi_compute.m: per condition, the condition's ERP removed (subtracterp.m with three conditions), 3-cycle Hanning windows at 10-ms steps ('mtmconvol'), PSI z per pair and time point against its own null (the Methods' frequency shuffle of one signal, as for the task-induced PSI), on the pairs with processing |z| > 1.96 under the same reading (the selection of directional-pairs). Main spectra: the 900-ms segment zero padded (Methods, Time-Resolved PSI, "Spectral decomposition ... otherwise identical"); variant: windows on the whole derived epoch, as psi_compute.m computes them. subtracterp.m selects the temporal trials with trialinfo(:,5)==2, the delay column, which selects none; the condition column (4) is used here. At each time point the mixed model (condition fixed, subject and pair random) is computed as the paired test over pairs (fcx3.paired_lme, checked against statsmodels below), FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg) over the 91 time points at 0.05, sustained when a run of significant points of one sign spans at least 100 ms (the runs longer than 100 ms are printed as well, for the Figure 5 legend's ">100 ms").

TIMES = np.round(RES[fcx3.SUBJECTS[0]]["power_toi"] * 1000).astype(int)
TCFG = {"methods": "segment zero-padded (main)", "code": "whole-epoch windows (psi_compute.m)"}
TR = {}
for config in fcx3.PSI_T_CONFIGS:
    for band in fcx3.BANDS:
        for k in ("a", "b"):
            z = {c: [] for c in (1, 2, 3)}
            subj, pair = [], []
            for sid in fcx3.SUBJECTS:
                names = [f"{sid}:{a}-{b}" for a, b, _ in RES[sid]["pairs"]]
                keep = np.array([nm in SEL[(band, k)] for nm in names])
                for c in (1, 2, 3):
                    z[c].append(RES[sid]["psi_t"][config][band][c][k][keep])
                subj += [sid] * int(keep.sum())
                pair += [nm for nm, kk in zip(names, keep) if kk]
            TR[(config, band, k)] = {"z": {c: np.concatenate(v) for c, v in z.items()}, "subject": np.array(subj), "pair": np.array(pair)}


def contrast_stats(config, band, k, other):
    d = TR[(config, band, k)]
    p, eff = [], []
    for ti in range(len(TIMES)):
        e, F, pv, n = fcx3.paired_lme(d["z"][other][:, ti], d["z"][1][:, ti], d["subject"])
        p.append(pv)
        eff.append(e)  # identity minus other
    p, eff = np.array(p), np.array(eff)
    sig = fcx3.fdr_bh(p) if len(d["subject"]) > 1 else np.zeros(len(TIMES), bool)
    runs = []
    for sign in (1, -1):
        for a, b in fcx3.runs(sig & (np.sign(eff) == sign), TIMES):
            runs.append((int(a), int(b), sign, int(b - a) >= 100))
    return p, eff, sig, sorted(runs)


def grand(config, band, k, c):
    d = TR[(config, band, k)]
    per = pd.DataFrame(d["z"][c]).groupby(d["subject"]).mean()
    return per.mean(axis=0).values, per.std(axis=0, ddof=1).values / np.sqrt(len(per)), per


STATS = {}
for config in fcx3.PSI_T_CONFIGS:
    for band in fcx3.BANDS:
        for k in ("a", "b"):
            for other, name in [(2, "spatial"), (3, "temporal")]:
                STATS[(config, band, k, name)] = contrast_stats(config, band, k, other)
                p, eff, sig, runs = STATS[(config, band, k, name)]

Result: reproduced, resting on PSI reading (a), and showing little. Under reading (a), adopted because its z is calibrated (see the task-induced PSI section and fig4c-alpha-beta-shift), the selection holds 78 pairs in 7 subjects and the grand means stay at or below 0.87 (spatial) and 1.01 (temporal), under 1.96 at every time point and under the paper's 1.60, which the criterion counts as reproduced. The absence shows little: under reading (a) the identity-trial grand mean also stays below 0.99, where the paper reports |z| above 2.35, so this measure shows no direction in any condition, and the 78 pairs are about as many as the trial-shuffled data select (68). Under reading (b) the selection leaves one pair (S1); its spatial-trial z reaches |z| = 3.07 (140 ms) and its temporal-trial z 2.36 (180 ms), with 16 and 11 of 91 time points at |z| >= 1.96, but its identity-trial z also passes 1.96 at 9 points, so on one pair such excursions are common. The second verification round reviewed not reproduced under reading (b); the change was proposed and the third round agreed. With the whole-epoch windows, reading (a) gives 0.37 and 0.56 and reading (b) 2.54 and 3.03.

            print(f"alpha-beta, {TCFG[config]}, {READ[k]}, identity vs {name}: FDR-significant points {int(sig.sum())}/91 (smallest p {p.min():.3g});"
                  f" runs {runs}; longest {longest} ms; sustained (>= 100 ms): {[r for r in runs if r[3]]}; (> 100 ms): {[r for r in runs if r[1] - r[0] > 100]}")

# subject-level test of the time-resolved contrasts: per subject the mean z over its selected pairs, a paired t-test
# over subjects at each time point, Benjamini-Hochberg over the 91 points (pairs that share electrodes are not counted
# as independent)
def subject_stats(config, band, k, other):
    d = TR[(config, band, k)]
    zi = pd.DataFrame(d["z"][1]).groupby(d["subject"]).mean()
    zo = pd.DataFrame(d["z"][other]).groupby(d["subject"]).mean()
    if len(zi) < 3:
        return None
    t, p = stats.ttest_rel(zi.values, zo.values, axis=0)
    sig = fcx3.fdr_bh(p)
    runs = [(int(a), int(b), sign) for sign in (1, -1) for a, b in fcx3.runs(sig & (np.sign(t) == sign), TIMES)]
    return len(zi), p, sig, sorted(runs)


for band in fcx3.BANDS:
    for config in fcx3.PSI_T_CONFIGS:
        for k in ("a", "b"):
            for other, name in [(2, "spatial"), (3, "temporal")]:
                r = subject_stats(config, band, k, other)
                if r is None:
                    print(f"{band}, {TCFG[config]}, {READ[k]}, identity vs {name}: fewer than 3 subjects, no test")
                    continue
                n, p, sig, runs = r
                print(f"{band}, {TCFG[config]}, {READ[k]}, identity vs {name}: {n} subjects; FDR-significant points {int(sig.sum())}/91"
                      f" (smallest p {p.min():.3g}); runs {runs}")
for k in ("a", "b"):
    d = TR[("methods", "alpha-beta", k)]
    print(f"alpha-beta pairs per subject, {READ[k]}:", pd.Series(d["subject"]).value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())

Result: partially reproduced, resting on PSI reading (a). Under reading (a), adopted (see fig4c-alpha-beta-shift; 104 pairs in 7 subjects), no point is significant after FDR in the pair-level model (smallest p 0.0015 and 0.0027) or in the subject-level test (0.016 and 0.024), under either spectra reading, the criterion's partial match. Under reading (b) (74 pairs in 6 subjects), 30 (identity against spatial) and 35 (against temporal) of 91 time points differ after FDR in the pair-level model, and the longest run of one sign lasts 40 ms (whole-epoch windows: 36 and 37 points, longest 50 and 40 ms). Those points come from the pair-level model alone. The 74 pairs are about as many as the trial-shuffled data select under the same reading (71), S3 supplies 44 of them, and the model treats pairs that share electrodes as independent; the paired test on the 6 subjects' means finds no point after FDR (smallest p 0.0029 and 0.0078). The second verification round reviewed reproduced under reading (b); the change was proposed and the third round agreed. No reading shows a sustained run.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Everything is computed in Python from the derived epochs; FieldTrip itself was not run. Windows, trial selection and spectral parameters follow the Methods and the deposited MATLAB scripts; where they differ, the Methods are the main reading and the scripts a variant. (1) ERP and power segments are zero padded as the Methods say; the scripts filter and transform the whole epoch, so that low-frequency windows take in the data around the segment. (2) The PSI null shuffles the frequencies of one signal and recomputes the same statistic, as the Methods say. psianalysis.m z-scores the mean of per-trial PSI against the slope of the trial-mean spectrum, a different statistic, and on trial-shuffled data that null gives |z| > 1.96 in 90% of pairs; it is shown as a variant. With the Methods' null the trial-shuffled data give 6 to 7% (reading (a)) and 0.1% (delta-theta) or 6% (alpha-beta) under reading (b), and the real data give few directional pairs, so none of the large PSI effects of the paper appears. (3) The cluster test's neighbours and alpha per tail are stated neither in the paper nor in the scripts, which hold no cluster test: the adjacency of contact numbers and 0.05 per tail are adopted, and every reading is shown. (4) PSI from trial-averaged cross-spectra (reading (a), Nolte et al. 2008) or per trial (reading (b)), each with one permutation for all trials or one per trial: reading (a) with one permutation for all trials is now adopted where the readings differ, because its z is calibrated on trial-shuffled and on synthetic independent data and reading (b)'s is not (its mean is offset by up to -1.25 per subject on the trial-shuffled data). Three outcomes verified under reading (b) were changed to what reading (a) gives, after a third verification round agreed: fig4c-alpha-beta-shift to not reproduced, fig5a-spatiotemporal-bidirectional to reproduced (an absence the measure shows in every condition), and fig5b-alpha-beta-no-sustained to partially reproduced. (5) The baseline z-score of power is computed in closed form; it cannot change the condition t-tests. (6) The mixed models are computed as paired tests over pairs, which equal them when every pair has both values (checked against statsmodels). As in the paper's degrees of freedom, pairs that share electrodes are treated as independent, which inflates the pair-level F; subject-level tests are printed beside them for the task-induced and the time-resolved PSI.

What was found about the data set. The derived epochs, the continuous data and the trial tables share one clock: every analysed channel's derived trace is a bipolar difference of two contacts of the continuous data (r >= 0.9998), at fixed offsets from the table's columns that put the scripts' windows where the Methods put them. The data set lists 187 analysed channels where the paper reports 192 (S4 has 5 parietal channels, Table 1 10), and 1135 same-hemisphere pairs where the paper reports 1129. The trial tables of S6 and S7 hold only the kept trials (101 and 90), unlike the description. A timing contrast between trials with 900-ms and 1150-ms delays shows, where the 70-150 Hz response is clear (S2, S3, S4), that the responses in the processing epoch of the 1150-ms trials occur 0.21 to 0.26 s later relative to the processing column than in the 900-ms trials, and in S4 the same in the encoding epoch, while the pretrial epochs of these subjects show shifts of 0.03 s or less; this is consistent with the encoding and processing columns being about 0.25 s early in 1150-ms trials, so that their processing window would include the end of the cue, but the test does not prove it and is weak in the other subjects (S1, S5 and S6 show shifts of 0.28 to 0.35 s that do not pass the shuffle test). The ERP and power tests and the task-induced PSI on the 900-ms-delay trials alone are shown as variants; power on those trials loses most effects, and so does power on a random draw of as many trials from both delays, so the loss reflects the smaller number of trials and the test cannot tell whether the timing matters. The deposited psi_compute.m does not run as written (an undefined freq and savDir, and an electrode argument tested with nargin > 2), subtracterp.m selects temporal trials by the delay column, which selects none, and psianalysis.m omits the conjugate of the cross-spectrum and z-scores against a null that is not the statistic it tests.
